note: All from strings are single lines copied from the files (several of these files use CRLF line endings, so no from string spans a line break). M7 needs both of its edits applied together (entry plus its 'also' edit): the route and the service each refuse the e-mail field on their own (defence in depth), so either edit alone is expected to survive. R2.2 and R3.7 likewise need their 'also' edits applied with the entry.

mutations.name: M2 restore an admin reset-password route that sets a password
mutations.expect: C4.1 (personas no longer all 404 NOT_FOUND), C4.2 (route inventory finds /:id/reset-password), C4.9 (R1's passwordHash changes)

mutations.name: M7 allow the admin e-mail change (refuseEmailField no-op and the service accepts email)

also.to:
if (payload.email !== undefined) await prisma.user.updateMany({ where: { id: userId, orgId }, data: { email: String(payload.email).trim().toLowerCase() } });
  if (false) {

mutations.expect: C4.8 (PATCH with email answers 200/403 instead of 400 USER_EMAIL_IDENTITY_OWNED; the home person's e-mail changes), C4.9

mutations.name: M13 the admin MFA-reset guard counts only active memberships elsewhere
mutations.to: where: { id: userId, orgId, memberships: { none: { orgId: { not: orgId }, status: "active" } } },
mutations.expect: C4.10 (the reset of a person only suspended in C succeeds instead of 403 IDENTITY_SHARED; the factor is cleared)

mutations.name: M16 sign-in with an unknown e-mail skips the dummy bcrypt compare
mutations.expect: C11.3 (unknown-e-mail median falls by the cost of one bcrypt-12 compare, far beyond the 60 ms bound)

mutations.name: M17 drop the credential-epoch check in routes/workspaces.js subjectOfToken
mutations.expect: C12.3 (old access and identity tokens open a B session), C12.5 (the old bearer is accepted as acceptance proof)

mutations.name: M18 drop the credential-epoch check for access tokens in middleware/auth.js authenticate
mutations.expect: C12.2 (the old access token still reads /auth/me and GET /projects)

mutations.name: M19 resetPassword stops bumping credentialEpoch
mutations.expect: C12.2, C12.3, C12.5, C12.6 (every pre-reset access and identity token stays valid)

mutations.name: M22 the emergency switch lets acceptance through
mutations.to: // (the emergency switch is not consulted at acceptance)
mutations.expect: C15.2 (accepting with AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_WRITE=false is no longer 503 MEMBERSHIP_WRITES_SUSPENDED; a User row is written and the link is consumed)

mutations.name: R2.1 createAuthSessionPayload no longer holds the proven epoch (the hold is dropped there; tokens still carry the proven epoch)
mutations.from: if (expectedEpoch !== null) await holdCredentialEpoch(tx, user.id, expectedEpoch);
mutations.to: // (the proven epoch is not held here)
mutations.expect: C12.9 (the workspace session waits on nothing: it answers 200 before the reset commits and writes a refresh session), C12.10 (200 and a refresh session written after the reset, its tokens at the old epoch)

mutations.name: R2.2 issueLoginOutcome mints at the epoch of the row it has just updated (its own hold dropped)

also.from: const payload = await createAuthSessionPayload(tx, updatedUser, context, { orgId: entry.orgId, expectedEpoch: provenEpoch });
also.to: const payload = await createAuthSessionPayload(tx, updatedUser, context, { orgId: entry.orgId, expectedEpoch: updatedUser.credentialEpoch });

mutations.expect: C12.11 (the sign-in waits at its lastLogin write instead, then mints at the new epoch: 200 with a live session and a refresh session written after the commit), C12.12 (the MFA completion likewise: 200 and a live session at the new epoch)

mutations.name: R2.3 routes/workspaces.js stops passing the token's epoch to issuance
mutations.from: { userId: req.tokenSubject.userId, orgId: req.params.orgId, ssoOrgId: req.tokenSubject.ssoOrgId, expectedEpoch: req.tokenSubject.epoch },
mutations.to: { userId: req.tokenSubject.userId, orgId: req.params.orgId, ssoOrgId: req.tokenSubject.ssoOrgId },
mutations.expect: C12.10 (issuance re-reads the row after the reset and holds the new epoch: 200 with a live session from the pre-reset token). C12.9 is expected to survive this one: there issuance reads the row while the reset is still uncommitted, so it holds the old epoch and is refused anyway

mutations.name: R2.4 POST /auth/reset-password stops dropping the person's live sockets
mutations.expect: C12.15 (the socket that joined the project room stays connected after the reset: no disconnect within 5 s)

mutations.name: R2.5 handleProjectJoin no longer compares the socket's credential epoch with the account's
mutations.expect: C12.16 (after the epoch moves under the socket, project:join answers ok: true and the socket stays connected)

mutations.name: R2.6 the admin MFA reset stops dropping the person's live sockets
mutations.expect: C12.17 (the person's socket stays connected after POST /company/security/users/:id/mfa/reset)

mutations.name: R2.7 an explicit PUBLIC_REGISTRATION=true opens registration under any NODE_ENV but exact production (the pre-fix behaviour)
mutations.to:
if (env.NODE_ENV !== "production" && String(env.PUBLIC_REGISTRATION ?? "").trim().toLowerCase() === "true") return true;
  if (!OPEN_BY_DEFAULT.has(String(env.NODE_ENV ?? "").trim().toLowerCase())) return false;
mutations.expect: C18.9 (staging, 'prod', '' and unset NODE_ENV with PUBLIC_REGISTRATION=true come back open). C18.8 is expected to survive: none of its cases sets the flag outside production

mutations.name: R2.8 resolveChallenge no longer compares the MFA challenge's epoch with the account's
mutations.from: if (!tokenEpochCurrent(payload, user)) throw new HttpError(401, "SESSION_REVOKED", "This session has ended; sign in again");
mutations.expect: C12.14 (the pre-reset challenge with a valid code answers 200 and writes a session at the new epoch)

mutations.name: R2.9 acceptance by an existing identity no longer holds the bearer's epoch
mutations.from: if (!reactivatesIdentity) await holdCredentialEpoch(tx, existingUser.id, Number.isInteger(identityEpoch) ? identityEpoch : -1);
mutations.to: if (!reactivatesIdentity) { /* (mutant) the bearer's epoch is not held */ }
mutations.expect: C12.13 (the acceptance waits at its User name write instead and then commits: 200 accepted with signInRequired, the link is used and the project assigned)

mutations.name: R3.1 a brand-new identity's acceptance issues without the epoch it wrote (ownEpoch back to null for a new identity, so issuance holds whatever the row says by then)
mutations.expect: C12.18 (issueWorkspaceSession reads the row after the committed bump and holds the new epoch: 200 with live tokens, a refresh session written for the new identity, no signInRequired). C12.13 survives (an existing identity still passes the bearer's epoch)

mutations.name: R3.2 the socket connection handler no longer re-checks the account after joining its rooms
mutations.expect: C12.19 (the handshake that read the pre-reset account stays connected in its rooms past 2 s and hears the probe addressed to the person)

mutations.name: R3.3 holdCredentialEpoch takes FOR SHARE again (the pre-R1 lock)
mutations.from: const rows = await tx.$queryRaw`SELECT "id" FROM "User" WHERE "id" = ${userId} AND "credentialEpoch" = ${epoch} AND "status" = 'active' FOR NO KEY UPDATE`;
mutations.to: const rows = await tx.$queryRaw`SELECT "id" FROM "User" WHERE "id" = ${userId} AND "credentialEpoch" = ${epoch} AND "status" = 'active' FOR SHARE`;
mutations.expect: C12.20 (the eight sign-ins released together all take the shared lock, then each one's lastLogin update waits on the others: deadlock victims answer 5xx instead of 200, fewer than 8 refresh sessions) and the final 'no answer was a 5xx' check. C12.21 survives (a workspace session does not update the User row)

mutations.name: R3.4 the self-service MFA enable writes the factor without the request's epoch
mutations.expect: C12.22 (the conditional write fails on the cleared seed instead and the request answers 409 MFA_STATE_CHANGED, not 401 SESSION_REVOKED). The from string is the 4-space-indented line of enable's writeOwnFactor call, the only one in the file

mutations.name: R3.5 the self-service MFA disable writes the factor without the request's epoch
mutations.from: await writeOwnFactor({ userId, epoch, expect: { mfaEnabled: true, passwordHash: user.passwordHash },
mutations.to: await writeOwnFactor({ userId, epoch: null, expect: { mfaEnabled: true, passwordHash: user.passwordHash },
mutations.expect: C12.23 (the conditional write fails on the changed password hash instead and the request answers 409 MFA_STATE_CHANGED, not 401 SESSION_REVOKED)

mutations.name: R3.6 the self-service MFA setup writes the pending seed without the request's epoch
mutations.from: await writeOwnFactor({ userId, epoch, expect: { mfaEnabled: false }, data: { mfaPendingSecretEnc: seal(secret) } });
mutations.to: await writeOwnFactor({ userId, epoch: null, expect: { mfaEnabled: false }, data: { mfaPendingSecretEnc: seal(secret) } });
mutations.expect: C12.24 (after the held epoch bump commits the setup answers 200 with a secret and a pending seed is written on the identity whose sessions just ended)

mutations.name: R3.7 the admin MFA reset awaits the notice e-mail before it returns (the pre-R3 order)

also.from: sendEmail({ to: user.email, ...templates.mfaResetNotice({ name: user.name }), metadata: { orgId, userId, type: "mfa_reset_notice" } })
also.to: return sendEmail({ to: user.email, ...templates.mfaResetNotice({ name: user.name }), metadata: { orgId, userId, type: "mfa_reset_notice" } })

mutations.expect: C12.25 (the reset answers only after the webhook's 8 s delay, far beyond the 2 s bound, and the route drops the socket only then). Both edits go together: the first runs the notice before returning, the second makes it return the delivery promise that is awaited
